aggressive_definition: Biopsy-detected high-grade or higher-stage prostate cancer, defined as Gleason score at least 4+4 or clinical tumor stage at least cT2b.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Among European American (EA) men, there was an association of 25-OH D <12 ng/mL with higher Gleason score ≥ 4+4 [OR, 3.66; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.41-9.50; P = 0.008] and tumor stage [stage ≥ cT2b vs. ≤ cT2a, OR, 2.42 (1.14-5.10); P = 0.008].
study_design: Prospective cross-sectional first-biopsy study of men with an abnormal prostate-specific antigen and/or digital rectal examination.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25-OH D) was obtained from 667 men, ages 40 to 79 years, prospectively enrolled from Chicago urology clinics undergoing first prostate biopsy.
reason: The abstract evaluates biopsy-detected incident prostate cancer and separately analyzes aggressive disease according to high Gleason score and higher clinical tumor stage. Prospective enrollment alone does not establish a longitudinal prospective cohort design.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: In African American (AA) men, we find increased odds of prostate cancer diagnosis on biopsy with 25-OH D < 20 ng/mL [OR, 2.43 (1.20-4.94); P = 0.01].
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied estimate is for any prostate cancer diagnosis on biopsy among African American men, not specifically high-grade or higher-stage disease.

additional_estimates.comparison: African American men with 25-OH D <12 ng/mL versus the reference category used in the study
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: AA men demonstrated an association between 25-OH D < 12 ng/mL and Gleason ≥ 4+4 [OR, 4.89 (1.59-15.07); P = 0.006].
additional_estimates.endpoint_definition: Biopsy-detected prostate cancer with Gleason score ≥4+4 among African American men
